design_history: v1 (one ML estimator for all targets, body/fuel features always on) failed acceptance on these held-out groups: served-target macro F1 0.73 vs milestone-lookup baseline 0.75 (data/reports/service_need_v1_rejected_evaluation.json). v2 adds a per-target choice between the ML model and a milestone-frequency estimator and a feature-set ablation, both decided only on inner training-group folds. Because v2 was designed after v1's held-out result was seen, its held-out metrics are optimistically biased; re-validate on new fleet service records.
target_meaning: 1 = the service item was performed at the recorded workshop visit. Scheduled-service need, not an observed or predicted failure.

group_split.time_aware_split: Not possible: the records have no visit dates or vehicle identifiers.

metrics.baseline: milestone_lookup (training-group service frequency at the nearest 10,000 km milestone, F1-tuned threshold)

cost_experiment.reason: Costs are Indian-rupee workshop prices from 2016-2018 for four models; they are not valid estimates for the fleet's currency, region or year. Fleet cost answers use the fleet's own recorded maintenance costs instead.

probability_validation.method: sigmoid (Platt) on out-of-fold predictions from leave-one-group-out training folds

acceptance_criteria.rules: macro balanced accuracy and macro F1 over served targets >= 0.60 and >= the milestone-lookup baseline; calibrated macro Brier below the prevalence baseline and ECE <= 0.15; >= 2 groups per split with zero overlap.

training_config.calibration: Platt scaling (GroupPlattCalibratedClassifier) on out-of-fold scores from leave-one-group-out training folds
training_config.threshold_rule: maximise F1 on out-of-fold calibrated probabilities from training groups

limitations: Four car models from two Indian cities, 2016-2018; no motorcycles, pickups, vans or minivans.
Targets are workshop service decisions, which largely follow manufacturer schedules; they are not wear measurements or failures.
No visit dates or vehicle IDs, so no service-window or failure-date estimate can be validated.
Vehicles outside the training domain (body type, fuel type, odometer range) are refused rather than extrapolated.
